text:
noah: heads up — we've had 3 incidents in the last 2 hours where inference pods stayed Pending for 6+ minutes while CA spun up GPU nodes. root cause looks like a mix of custom-metrics timeouts and nodeSelector mismatches. logs attached below.

shivani: ugh. saw the same. metrics-adapter returning 503s under peak QPS, so HPA didn't get current gpu_queue_length and stayed at the old replica count. CA saw Pending pods and scaled up, but because our nodepool label is `gpu:true` and some new nodes come up with `gpu:v2` pool label, pods failed scheduling for a bit.

mike: confirming — snippet from kube-scheduler:
```
I0310 14:05:13.234567       1 scheduler_predicates.go:123] Pod default/inference-x unschedulable: node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
I0310 14:05:18.998100       1 scheduler_binder.go:87] Pod default/inference-x failed binding: no matching node labels (required: nvidia.com/gpu=true)
```

noah: here's the HPA we deploy for the inference worker (shortened):
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 24
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: gpu_queue_length
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "50"
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
```

shivani: adapter logs show intermittent timeouts to Prometheus on our prometheus-adapter pods when queries spike: `GET /api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time... 504` — causes HPA to treat metric as unavailable. HPA then uses previous value (stale) and delays scaling.

scale-bot: cluster-autoscaler: ScaleUp: setting group: gpu-pool-us-west +3 (max 10) — reason: >=1 pod(s) didn't fit.

eva: a few follow-ups:
- we have two GPU pools with slightly different labels because of a rollout (gpu=true vs gpu:v2). CA can create nodes in either, but our k8s podSpec uses `nodeSelector: { "nvidia.com/gpu": "true" }` which excludes v2 nodes. mismatch window ~120s where CA thinks it's helping but scheduler still can't place pods.
- metrics adapter flakiness + HPA stabilizationWindow doubles the delay.

samir: quick mitigation options:
- relax nodeSelector to accept both labels (or add toleration/affinity) so new nodes are usable immediately.
- switch HPA to use External metrics with lower `periodSeconds` and set `tolerance` tighter.
- OR use CA warm-pool so nodes are provisioned faster (pre-warmed) — reduces scale-up latency from ~3m to ~30s.

mike: +1 for warm-pool. Also consider enabling `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` if CA is aggressively trying to balance and picks wrong group. but beware side effects.

shivani: long-term: we should move to a push-based external metric for queue length (gateway that pushes to external metrics API) instead of relying on heavy PromQL queries under QPS spikes. reduces adapter load.

noah: another immediate band-aid: lower HPA stabilizationWindow for scaleUp (it's currently defaulting) and increase `behavior.scaleUp.policies` to allow faster ramp (but keep a cap). Example suggestion: `type: Percent value: 100 periodSeconds: 60` to double replicas in a minute.

scale-bot: NOTE: recent deploy changed nodepool label for gpu-pool-eu -> `nvidia.com/gpu=v2`. Rollback candidate flagged.

eva: action items:
1) shivani to add a short-lived fix to adapter: increase Prometheus replica count and add read-timeout tuning (ETA 2h).
2) samir to create PR to accept both gpu label variants in podSpec or add a compatibility label on new nodes (ETA 1d).
3) infra to enable warm-pool on critical gpu-pools for scale test (ops ticket #4589).
4) short RFC to evaluate push-based external metrics vs Prometheus queries (volunteer: mike).

samir: also update CA config: set `--max-node-provision-time` lower? careful, that's a hard threshold. maybe tweak `scale-down-unneeded-time` and `scale-down-utilization-threshold` first.

noah: sounds good. thanks all — let's track in infra board. if we see another incident, escalate to paging. :thumbsup:

mike: quick PR for podSpec compatibility in flight: will link once ready.

shivani: increased prometheus-adapter from 2->4 replicas in staging, monitoring for 30m.

scale-bot: cluster-autoscaler: ScaleUp event resolved, nodes became Ready after 1m 45s (provisioning delay decreased due to prewarm).

noah: closing loop — after the adapter scale and label change we saw one more spike but pods scheduled within 45s. keeping warm-pool enabled for now.

(threads end)
